sources: Load all eight completed E24 merging/non-merging states and verify SHA-256 identities against the recorded E24 audit. Preserve every persistent expert plus any retained temporary expert, its optimizer, context and reservoir. Freeze expert parameters. Pool only actual observed records from per-module anchors and any live scratch reservoir; no simulator/audit targets enter fitting. Baseline active selection uses exactly the existing active or temporary predictor. Cases with one expert have no selection problem and bypass router construction/fitting explicitly.
routing: Standardize inputs using pooled memory mean and population standard deviation clamped at 0.1. Compute each frozen expert's squared error on observed noisy memory targets and label each record by its lowest-error expert. Nearest-anchor predicts that expert label for the closest standardized memory input. The top-one router is 8-to-16-tanh-to-K, trained by cross-entropy on the same labels. The mixture router has the same architecture, trained on squared error of softmax-weighted cached expert predictions against observed memory targets. Both use Adam 0.01 for 256 batches of 64 sampled with replacement. No checkpoint selection, hidden region flag, query outcome or E24 probe feedback is used. Top-one selection runs only the selected expert for each query; the mixture evaluates all K experts. The mixture may outperform the best single expert, so hard-expert diagnostics are not universal lower bounds.
queries: Reconstruct each fixed E24 teacher only in the evaluator. Use independent query RNG seed source_seed+900000 for original support and +910000 for shifted support; all router arms consume identical paired queries. Common inputs sample all four previously observed common means; rare inputs use the original zero mean. The shifted law multiplies the seven non-marker coordinates by 1.5 and adds a fixed fresh Gaussian shift of scale 1.5. The marker coordinate retains the E24 sign/magnitude law. Eight phases change query frequencies within each fixed retrieval assay; the router and experts do not learn during evaluation. Report whole, rare/common and phase errors, including every failure. Stream length here is repeated retrieval, not an autonomous planning horizon.
diagnostics: Record per-example best retained expert error and best single expert mean for each region, explicitly privileged and never used by the router. Unlike E24's best-persistent-only diagnostic, E25 includes a retained temporary expert when present. Compare original support and shifted support separately. A recovered access gap does not demonstrate restoration of information absent from every retained expert. No comparison selects a best router per source using query labels as an operational arm.
preflight: Verify source identities, frozen experts and unchanged source counters/state, exact active predictions, one-expert bypass equality, nearest-anchor labels at distinct stored inputs, actual learned parameter change, exact restored router predictions, soft-mixture finite-difference gradient, and query causality. Use synthetic dummy experts and disjoint preflight data for router functional checks. Count expert evaluations used to make memory targets and every fitted router forward/backward batch.
costs: Retain inherited E24 learner tensor and parameter counts, optimizers and reservoirs. Add routing parameters, optimizer moments, normalization tensors and any duplicated standardized-memory/label cache. Charge K*N expert examples for fitting-target construction, 256*64 router training examples and 256 backward/optimizer steps, plus actual query routing, expert examples and nearest-neighbor distance comparisons. Active and one-expert arms bypass target construction. Report fit and query loop time, construction time, source loading and inherited E24 loop work separately; source creation is not free. Cached training predictions are transient and their bytes are recorded, not silently persistent after fitting. Source and query data shared across arms do not create independent observations. Full process/peak autograd RAM, complete FLOPs, energy and latency amortization beyond this finite assay remain unmeasured.
falsification: If observed-memory-trained routing fails fresh rare/common queries, an audit's privileged best-module gap has not been converted into a usable capability. If nearest-anchor matches or beats the learned router, credit the simpler retrieval mechanism. Losses after support shift remain failures even if original support improves. If source merging left one inadequate model, bypassing selection must retain that limitation. This is a frozen-state causal access test, not continual learning, recursive improvement, new world knowledge, general reasoning, novel mixture-of-experts theory or full architecture completion. A positive retrieval repair must next survive actual online model/memory changes and repay fitting/access costs.
